source: Payroll and billing conventions: a weekly pay cycle is 52 paydays a year, a fortnightly one 26, a semimonthly one 24 (two a month), a monthly one 12; a bill is drawn on the day it is due; a pay-later instalment is a bill due on its day; spending with no date is spread evenly over the month's days.
confidenceNote: Nothing here is a measurement. Paydays a month is arithmetic on the cycle (52 ÷ 12, 26 ÷ 12, 2, 1); the timing rules are the simplest honest reading of a month, and the room says so in its assumptions drawer. A person's real bank draws a bill a day or two around its due date, and a weekly pay cycle lands five paydays in some months and four in others — the month drawn here is the average one.
note: the pay cadences and the bill-timing conventions a month is drawn with (Money Calendar & Pay-Later)
